threads.body: [Javaagent] If iterating an asynchronous bulk request's key collection throws, request construction exits after incrementing call depth but before returning an `AdviceScope`. The suppressed exception leaves exit advice unable to decrement the depth, so subsequent Spymemcached calls on that thread are treated as nested and produce no spans. Roll back the increment when request/listener construction fails, and add a regression test that follows a failed bulk capture with a normal request.

replies.body: Fixed in 249b639a. Failed request/listener construction now decrements call depth before rethrowing to the advice suppression boundary. The regression follows failed bulk capture with a normal async get and verifies that the later request still emits a span.

@copilot Update this PR directly with a focused follow-up for the query-capture lifecycle defect identified in https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20943#discussion_r4368992947. The canonical getBulk(Collection, Transcoder) simplification in 90b9f328 is delivered and should remain unchanged.

In MemcachedClientInstrumentation.AdviceScope.start, the outermost call increments CallDepth before SpymemcachedRequest.create and listener construction. Query sanitization now iterates application bulk-key collections and can throw. When construction fails, entry advice suppresses that exception without returning an AdviceScope, so exit advice cannot balance the increment and later Spymemcached calls on the same thread stop producing spans. Balance the increment on request/listener construction failure before the exception reaches the existing advice suppression boundary. Preserve the nested-call bookkeeping and normal completion behavior; do not silently turn the failure into successful query capture or change application exception behavior.

Add focused regression coverage proving that failed bulk capture cannot suppress a later normal request on the same thread. Prefer an installed-agent test exercising the real entry/exit suppression path if practical. Keep the canonical synchronous bulk snapshot, asynchronous completion/cancellation behavior, iterator omission, value redaction, query-length limit, operation names, and CAS handling intact. Do not resolve or reply to review threads; the coordinator will verify the fix and handle the review thread.

Apply the narrowest relevant Spotless formatter directly before behavioral validation and run the focused regression plus existing bulk overload/cancellation coverage. Commit and push only this focused correction to this PR's existing head branch.

[Javaagent] The `asyncGetBulk(Collection<String>, Iterator<Transcoder<T>>)` overload requests only the minimum of the key and transcoder counts, explicitly allowing unequal lengths. With keys `[key1, key2]` and one transcoder, this loop emits `getBulk key1 key2` even though only `key1` is requested. Omit keys for this overload, as for iterator-supplied keys, unless the actually consumed keys can be captured without advancing either iterator.

replies.body: Fixed in 249b639a. The collection/iterator-transcoder overload now omits keys without advancing either iterator. Regression coverage includes unequal key/transcoder counts and iterator non-consumption, and the README documents this limitation.

threads.body: [Javaagent] Closing the async advice scope restores the outer `SyncBulkAdvice` context, making its bulk snapshot available again. If a synchronous bulk read runs a custom `Transcoder.decode()` on the caller thread and that decoder performs an `asyncGetBulk` lookup, the nested lookup records the outer request's keys instead of its own. Make the snapshot a one-use handoff to the delegated async call so later reentrant bulk requests sanitize their own arguments.

replies.body: Fixed in 249b639a. The synchronous snapshot is now a one-use handoff consumed with getAndSet(null), so restoring the outer scope cannot expose its keys again. The reentrant-decoder regression verifies that outer and nested bulk requests retain their own query text.

@copilot Implement and push the following focused query-capture corrections directly to this PR. The prior correction session 50007793-be25-41f3-8756-b3298aa38026 ended without a commit or reply; the live head is still 90b9f328b9cd2597e3ddd8bd9fdfa3cb28f97cb4, and none of these issues is fixed. Preserve the delivered simplification that SyncBulkAdvice matches only getBulk(Collection, Transcoder). This is a coding request, not an analysis-only request.

Fix the call-depth leak identified at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20943#discussion_r4368992947. In MemcachedClientInstrumentation.AdviceScope.start, balance the outermost CallDepth increment if request/listener construction throws before an AdviceScope is returned. Keep exception reporting/suppression at the existing advice boundary and preserve normal and nested-call bookkeeping. Add a regression that exercises failed bulk capture followed by a normal request on the same thread and verifies that the later span is still emitted.

Fix misleading keys for asyncGetBulk(Collection<String>, Iterator<Transcoder<T>>) as described at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20943#discussion_r4369036683. Spymemcached 2.12.0 explicitly permits unequal iterator lengths and loops while keyIter.hasNext() && tcIter.hasNext(), so not every collection key is necessarily requested. Omit captured keys for this explicit iterator-transcoder overload without advancing either iterator. Continue capturing keys for ordinary collection/transcoder and varargs overloads. Cover the unequal-length case and iterator non-consumption, and update the existing README limitation briefly if needed.

Fix reentrant snapshot reuse as described at https://github.com/open-telemetry/opentelemetry-java-instrumentation/pull/20943#discussion_r4369036714. The BULK_QUERY_TEXT snapshot is currently restored when the delegated async advice scope closes, so a caller-thread Transcoder.decode callback performing a different asyncGetBulk can pick up the outer synchronous request's keys. Make the snapshot a one-use handoff to the delegated async request while retaining correct scope cleanup. This is a supported path: TranscodeService.Task.get invokes run on the caller, and BulkGetFuture.internalGet calls those decode futures' get methods. Add focused regression coverage proving that a reentrant bulk lookup records its own keys, not the consumed outer snapshot.

Keep these changes limited to the query-capture lifecycle and key accuracy. Preserve async completion/cancellation semantics, iterator-key omission, value redaction, the length limit, operation names, and descriptor-based CAS handling. Apply the narrowest relevant Spotless formatter immediately before behavioral validation. Run the new regressions plus existing bulk overload/cancellation coverage. Commit and push the fixes to this PR's existing head branch.

@copilot Update this PR directly with the sanitizer readability proposal below. The user's request was: "if (operation.equals(\"getBulk\") && descriptor.startsWith(\"(Ljava/util/Collection;Ljava/util/Iterator;\")) { ... (descriptor.startsWith(\"(Ljava/lang/String;JI\")) { ... Uh, is there a better way to do this, or at least could we add some comments to make this method easier to read kind of the whole method". They then invoked /cloud for the proposal.

Limit the change to instrumentation/spymemcached-2.12/javaagent/src/main/java/io/opentelemetry/javaagent/instrumentation/spymemcached/v2_12/SpymemcachedQuerySanitizer.java. Keep the descriptor-based overload discrimination and preserve behavior exactly. Extract the two encoded signature checks into private static boolean predicates named hasPerKeyTranscoders(String descriptor) and hasCasExpiration(String descriptor). Document the corresponding Java parameter layouts next to the encoded strings: asyncGetBulk(Collection keys, Iterator transcoders), and cas/asyncCAS(String key, long cas, int expiration, Object value, ...). Keep the same descriptor prefixes; do not add descriptor parsing, reflection, dependencies, a command framework, or a helper per switch branch.

Move the getBulk iterator-transcoder guard into case "getBulk", so the bulk behavior is together. At its call site, explain that this overload requests only as many keys as there are transcoders, and determining which keys are requested would consume the iterator. Preserve omission of iterator-supplied keys and do not consume key or transcoder iterators. Preserve Collection and String[] handling, including the transcoder preceding the varargs key array.

At the CAS predicate call site, explain why declared parameter types are required: a numeric stored value must not be mistaken for an expiration. Keep key, CAS token, optional expiration, and masked value in precisely the same order.

Make the rest of sanitize readable with short comments describing the non-obvious argument layouts of the grouped cases. set/add/replace take key, expiration, stored value, and optional transcoder. append/prepend may start with a primitive long CAS token before the key and always mask the appended/prepended value. incr/decr take key, delta, optional initial value, optional expiration; mask the initial value while retaining delta and expiration. get/gets/getAndTouch/touch/delete may have a second numeric argument for expiration or deletion delay; ignore transcoders. Explain that the default branch deliberately omits unknown-operation arguments to avoid exposing values. Comment the code as it is now, without describing this change or adding obvious line-by-line narration.

Leave sanitizeBulk, append, truncation, query formats, operation naming, advice/lifecycle code, and tests unchanged. Preserve all current PR work, including direct unprefixed test keys, exact telemetry assertions, suite wiring, and the user's unconditional Testcontainers build-service registration. The user explicitly chose to keep the README unchanged after the previous privacy-note review; do not restore or add that note.

Run the narrowest relevant spotlessApply task immediately before behavioral validation, then run the existing SpymemcachedQuerySanitizerTest suite, including its numeric-CAS and iterator regressions. Commit and push this focused change to the existing PR head branch. Do not post review replies or resolve threads; the coordinator handles those after verification.
